target_customer: Active consumers who buy personalized protein and sports nutrition by subscription, later also via Target retail
problem: Off-the-shelf protein powders do not match individual goals and diets. Gainful uses a quiz and dietitian support to tailor blends.
business_model: DTC subscription of personalized supplements, plus retail (Target) from 2023

founders.name: Jahaan Ansari
education: UC Berkeley, finishing degrees in Computer Science and Chemical Engineering in 2017
founders.background_notes: Source: AlleyWatch (Jan 2021). High school soccer teammate of Eric Wu.

founders.name: Eric Wu
founders.background_notes: AlleyWatch says he started the company at age 21 and was 25 at the time of the article. TechCrunch (2021-01-13) says he shifted from CEO to COO and that Dean Kelly became chief executive in an early 2020 transition. The YC page lists only Ansari.

technical_complexity.rationale: A quiz driven recommendation engine and a subscription storefront on top of contract manufactured powders. Operational complexity in sourcing and fulfillment exceeds software difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Personalization data and dietitian service differentiate, but the model could be copied by other DTC supplement brands. The company claims over one hundred million proprietary data points on its site, a self claim.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Gainful. Care/of launched customizable protein powders in March 2019 per Gear Patrol, after the YC batch.

market_need_then: AlleyWatch (2021) quotes the founders on generic off-the-shelf supplements not fitting individual needs. No 2018 dated demand statistics were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses gainful.com, the exact name as .com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Wordmark, details not described by sources
identity.visual_style: Clean supplement packaging with flavor packets

branding.brand_signature: Unflavored protein paired with swappable flavor packets

brand_strength.rationale: Reached Target distribution in 2023 and product review coverage exists, but no sourced evidence of community, memes or merch.

outcome_analysis: Gainful grew a personalized protein subscription business after YC Winter 2018, raised a $7.5 million Series A in January 2021, changed CEO in early 2020 with Dean Kelly joining, and expanded into hydration and pre-workout lines. A profile reports profitability in early 2023 and a launch in Target stores, which suggests a capital efficient path with retail distribution. No exit has been reported.
notes: Series A confirmed by TechCrunch (Jan 13, 2021), NutraIngredients (Jan 14, 2021) and AlleyWatch. NutraIngredients reports $7.6M total equity raised; a 2026 profile says $11M, unverified. A convertible note at the start of the pandemic (amount undisclosed) is recorded as an other round. Seedtable and Crunchbase list a roughly $120K seed with conflicting dates, treated as unverified and not recorded. Competitors: Care/of (March 2019, Gear Patrol) and Kyoku and Buddy Nutrition (2018 to 2019 launches) found only in sources after the batch window, so the list is empty. Founders Eric Wu and Jahaan Ansari are named by TechCrunch and NutraIngredients although the YC page lists only Ansari. Profitability and Target claims come from secondary profiles.
